title: Minimum Cost Climbing Stairs
statement: A staircase charges a toll per stair: cost[i] (a non-negative integer) is the fee you pay at the moment you step on stair i. From any stair you may hop up 1 or 2 stairs per move. Your goal is the landing just past the top stair (one position beyond index len(cost)-1); the landing itself is free. You may begin at either stair 0 or stair 1 (you only pay for a stair once you step on it, including your starting stair). Return the minimum total fee (an int) to reach the landing. The input list always has at least 2 stairs.
hints: The cheapest way to stand on stair i only depends on the cheapest ways to stand on the two stairs below it. Does that suggest a table you can fill left to right?

Let dp[i] = minimum total fee paid if your last step landed on stair i. Base cases: dp[0] = cost[0] and dp[1] = cost[1], since you can start on either for just its own fee. Recurrence: dp[i] = cost[i] + min(dp[i-1], dp[i-2]).
Fill dp for i from 2 to n-1. The landing sits one past the top, and you can hop 1 or 2, so your final paid stair is either n-1 or n-2 — return min(dp[n-1], dp[n-2]), not dp[n-1] alone.
